articleTitle: Maximizing the Power Transfer for a Mixed Inductive and Capacitive Wireless Power Transfer System
abstract: Nowadays, near-field wireless power transfer is realized by inductive or capacitive coupling. Power transmission is respectively accomplished by a time-varying magnetic or electric field as medium. Recently, mixed or hybrid near-field wireless power transfer is being developed as a possible mean to increase the power density of the system by utilizing both the magnetic and the electric near-field. The fundamental basics of mixed coupling are well understood. However, the implications of the mixed coupling theory on wireless power transfer applications is not rigorously described. Moreover, no general description is available that allows for a detailed comparison between current hybrid systems, especially for a series topology of inductive and capacitive coupling. In this work, we analytically solve a general mixed wireless power transfer configuration with series topology. We determine the optimal load to maximize the amount of power transfer and calculate the maximum achievable output power. The analytical derivation is validated by numerical simulation in SPICE. Our solution provides insight in the mixed wireless link and can serve as a reference point to evaluate the performance of mixed systems with regard to power transfer.

articleTitle: Dual-band Rectenna Using Voltage Doubler Rectifier and Four-Section Matching Network
abstract: A dual-frequency rectenna is introduced in this paper. An enhanced-gain antenna is integrated with the rectifying circuit for increasing the rectenna capability for scavenging. A voltage doubler circuit is used for the rectification. Moreover, a four-section matching network is employed for the matching between the antenna and the rectifier. The measured results reveal that the RF-to-DC conversion efficiency is more than 50% over wide range of the input power, from-3.5dBm to 10. 5dBm at f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> and from -4.5dBm to 11dBm at f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, with maximum conversion efficiency of 63% and 69% at input power of 7dBm and 3. 5dBm, respectively with resistive load of 1KΩ. Further-more, the measurements illustrate good agreement between the simulated and measured results.

articleTitle: Optimal Operation of Multitone Waveforms in Low RF-Power Receivers
abstract: This paper presents a study of the optimal performance of multitone signals in low RF-power transfer and energy harvesters. The choice of the load can be tricky, showing an advantage of a certain type of signals over another. For low RF power (-17dBm), the multitone signals do not improve the peak RF-to-dc power conversion efficiency (PCE) over the continuous wave (CW) single-tone signal, if the optimal load is selected for each case, however, the multitone signals maintain that peak PCE of ~ 47% over higher output voltage (i.e: larger loads), and consequently enable more efficient dc-to-dc voltage boosting or even eliminate the need for the voltage booster in the RF power receiver. Thus, the low-power multitone waveforms can be considered as a voltage sensitivity booster rather than a PCE efficiency booster. This boosted rectified voltage is the key advantage of the multitone signals that leads to the enhancement in the overall efficiency of the low-RF power receiver.

articleTitle: Towards the Improvement of Frequency-domain Chipless RFID Readers
abstract: Chipless RFID readers widely use two antennas for the interrogation of the tag and reception of the response, making them heavy and bulky. Also, the strong self-jamming leakage signal degrades the sensitivity of the reader, and compromises the maximum reading range of the system. Furthermore, FCC regulatory restrictions for UWB applications makes FMCW readers unlikely as a practical solution in such technology. Herein, we propose a single-antenna LSFCW chipless RFID reader enabled with a self-interference compensation unit and an enhanced signal generation technique to address the above constraints. The proposed solution holds great promise for commercial adoption of this technology, particularly for handheld devices.

articleTitle: Butterfly-Shaped Transmitting Coil for Wireless Power Transfer System in Millimeter-Sized Biomedical Implants
abstract: This paper presents a new butterfly-shaped transmitting (BS-Tx) coil of a magnetic resonance wireless power transfer (WPT) system for miniaturized biomedical implants. The range and misalignment tolerances are the main factors, which result in transfer efficiency degradation. The proposed BS-Tx coil improves the efficiency despite variations in the distance, angle, and axial misalignment with a 9-mm diameter receiver coil. A wireless power transfer efficiency exhibits a significant improvement as compared to a conventional WPT system under the same conditions.

articleTitle: Wireless Charging of Electric Vehicles
abstract: Wireless charging of electric vehicles (EVs) has been in development for several years in preparation for the growth in adoption of these vehicles. Wireless charging systems today offer an efficient, flexible means of charging EVs from multiple classes and at a range of power levels from a common ground source. Standardization activities are well underway to ensure compatibility between systems across vehicle makers and location. This paper provides a snapshot of wireless charging technology as applied to EVs.

articleTitle: Maximum Transfer Efficiency of MIMO-WPT System
abstract: In this paper, a novel universal method to calculate the maximum power transfer efficiency for arbitrary multiple input multiple output wireless power transfer (MIMO-WPT) system is presented by using multiport impedance matrix. The method can be applied to evaluate the maximum transfer efficiency of any types of transmitting and receiving elements, and obtain the optimum impedance as well. The effectiveness and flexibility of the new approach will be demonstrated by applying some MIMO-WPT systems.

articleTitle: A Multi-MHz IPT-link Developed for Load Characterisation at Highly Variable Coupling Factor
abstract: This paper presents the development and characterisation of an inductive link to assess and compare inductive power transfer (IPT) systems that operate at 6.78 or 13.56 MHz. First, the properties of two equal air-core coils were obtained from simulations and corroborated experimentally. Then, the coupling factor between the coils was calculated in function of separation and misalignment. A receiving-end circuit, comprised of a capacitance and a resistive load, was also characterised in order to reflect different loads to the transmitter at different tunings and couplings, and therefore represent the effects produced by changes in coupling and variations in the rectifier's input impedance. The link was tested, firstly using a Class E inverter and then a load-independent Class EF inverter, both at power levels lower than 200 W. The reflected load was changed by altering coupling, and the tuning capacitance. A comparison between these inverter topologies handling highly reactive loads is shown here for the first time.

articleTitle: History of Research and Development of Beam Wireless Power Transfer
abstract: This paper aims to describe the history of research and development (R &D) of beam wireless power transfer (WPT) via microwaves. Starting in the 1960s, many interesting beam WPT field experiments have been conducted worldwide. The R&D of the beam WPT walked along a solar power satellite (SPS). The beam efficiency from a transmitting antenna to a receiving antenna is one of the most important parameter of the beam WPT. In this paper, the history is reviewed and future perspectives of the WPT are described.

articleTitle: Compact Dual-Band Wireless Power Transfer Using Overlapped Single Loop Defected Ground Structure
abstract: This paper presents a compact dual-band wireless power transfer (WPT) system using overlapped defected ground structure for biomedical applications. One band for power and another for data transfer. The proposed defected ground structure can channel two distinct resonant frequencies. As a result, the fabricated WPT device has almost 50% reduction in the size without changing other performances compared to ref. [9]. The fabricated device is 15 mm ×15 mm. The measured efficiency is 71% and 73%, respectively at 0.45 GHz and 0.95 GHz at WPT distance of 12.5mm.

articleTitle: Array Pattern Synthesis of Flat-topped Beam for Microwave Power Transfer System at Volcanoes
abstract: Microwave power transfer (MPT) is one of the wireless power transfer (WPT) technologies, which is of great advantage to beam forming and power transmission at middle-to-long distance as compared to other technologies. We suggest the MPT systems at volcanoes where a drone is employed as a point supplying microwave power. In this paper, we design a transmitting array antenna installed on the drone for flat-topped beams using Woodward Lawson method. This method is often used for beam forming in the field of wireless communication. However, the discussion including energy transmission efficiency has not been done, while it is indispensable to WPT application. Therefore, we evaluate the flat-topped beams obtained by this method from the viewpoints of both transmission efficiency and flatness and then find the suitable beam patterns for our system at both of 2.45GHz and 5.8GHz.

articleTitle: Size-adjustable Coils for Compensation of Lateral Misalignment in WPT Systems
abstract: This work demonstrates the feasibility of size-adjustable coils to minimize the reduction of the transfer efficiency due to the lateral misalignment between the source and load coils in a resonant-type wireless power transfer system. Experimental results for a 6.78 MHz system reveals that by reducing the size of the coil adaptively according to the misalignment, the transfer efficiency can be maintained above 80% even when effective overlapping area is reduced to 11.5% between a 20 × 20 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> coil pair. Moreover, the proposed coil system successfully removes the transfer null caused by a large misalignment. The proposed virtual system is expected to maintain the transfer efficiency higher than 40% even when the misalignment is such that one coil is completely outside the other.

articleTitle: Design, Simulation and Measurement of Flexible PCB Coils for Wearable Device Wireless Power Transfer
abstract: In this paper, we design and analyze flexible wireless power transfer (WPT) coils for flexible wearable devices. The 3 cm by 3 cm flexible coils are designed using polyimide substrate. The coil is designed as thin as possible to achieve higher Q-factor and power transfer efficiency (PTE). Furthermore, we analyzed the mutual inductance between the coils with a bending radius of a receiver (Rx) coil of infinite, 26 mm and 13 mm by considering the curvature of the human wrist. As the results, the simulation results of the flexible coil are verified with the measurement results using Z-parameter analysis in the frequency range from 1 MHz to 50 MHz. In conclusion, we verify the mutual inductance simulation results with the measurement results within the average error of 2.85%.

articleTitle: A Highly Sensitive Broadband Rectenna for Low Power Millimeter-wave Energy Harvesting Applications
abstract: In this paper, a highly sensitive broadband millimeter-wave energy harvesting rectenna has been designed, fabricated, and experimentally investigated. The proposed structure includes a high gain 8-by-1 gap-coupled antenna array and a zero-bias Schottky diode rectifier circuit, to efficiently convert RF to DC signal. In order to further characterize the antenna array circuit, both structures (antenna and rectifier) are individually implemented on thin-film ceramic substrate (ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> = 9.9, h = 127 μm), using an MHMIC (Miniature Hybrid Microwave Integrated Circuits) fabrication process. Then, they are joined together using low-loss wideband waveguide (WR12) to microstrip transitions in order to validate the investigated rectenna configuration. A maximum measured RF to DC conversion efficiency of 49.3 %, and sensitivity level of around -60 dBm were successfully achieved. These results make the proposed rectenna structure an excellent candidate for low power millimeter-wave energy harvesting.

articleTitle: High FOM Dual Band Wireless Power Transfer using Bow-tie Defected Ground Structure Resonators
abstract: This work presents a dual-band wireless power transfer (WPT) system with high figure of merit (FoM). One band can be used for power transfer and another for data transfer in biomedical applications. A Bow-tie Defected Ground Structure (DGS) resonators with high quality (Q-) factor and coupling (k-) factor is utilized for ensuring high efficiency. An equivalent circuit model using the admittance (J-) inverters is utilized to design the admittance inversion and compensation networks. The measured result shows that the proposed WPT system is able to transfer the power at both of the bands with a high FoM, making a suitable candidate for compact near filed WPT applications.

articleTitle: 13.56MHz 50W Load-Independent Synchronous Class E Rectifier using GaN devices for Space-Constrained Applications
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a load-independent synchronous Class E rectifier to enable fast and efficient wireless charging in space-constrained applications such as drones and laptops. Load-independent operation allows Class E circuits to maintain zero-voltage switching (ZVS) and a inherently regulated output voltage for any load value without the need for tuning or replacement of components. Load-independent operation also the allows Class E rectifiers to have a constant input reactance that does not vary with loading and coupling. This feature allows the rectifier to present a real impedance to the transmitter side and therefore allows the complete system to operate without detuning of the inverter or the wireless link. Operating at MHz switching frequencies is now possible with the availability of wide-bandgap devices such as GaN resulting in low profile, power dense converters to be realised. Here we present the design process and implementation of a 13.56 MHz 50W load-independent synchronous Class E rectifier using GaN devices for a wireless charging system operating at 13.56 MHz. The derivation of the switching signal and the circuitry to achieve this will also be discussed and initial experimental results will be presented.

articleTitle: Validation of the Design of an 11 kW Inductive Charging Prototype on a New Test Bench for WPT-Systems
abstract: In the future, different types of e-mobility will dominate the mobility. For a gain in comfort and range electrical vehicles (EV) can be equipped with an inductive charging system. For the development of inductive charging systems environments for testing are needed. In this paper a new designed test bench for an entire EV with an integrated inductive charging system is presented. Especially the testing of misalignment and the consideration of the vehicles underfloor can be realized very easy. With the aid of the new test bench, an 11kW prototype which was designed in a former paper will be measured and parameters will be compared with the designed parameters. The progress in testing infrastructure will lead to a faster and easier development of new prototypes.

articleTitle: Isolated Cuk Converter with Two Symmetrical Output voltages For SRM Drive
abstract: In this paper, a high power factor based isolated dual output Cuk converter fed SRM drive is proposed. The selected converter is featured with two equal output power sources, DC isolation and improved power quality operation over a complete input voltage range and loading conditions. To obtain input current shaping, DCM (Discontinuous Conduction Mode) of operation is selected, which presents the most simple and low cost control as compared to CCM (Continuous Conduction Mode), and CRM (critical conduction mode). It has resulted in the reduced size and cost of magnetic structure considerably. The speed control of proposed drive is based upon DC link voltage control, which is obtained by modulating pulse width of the Cuk converter. Experimental results of a prototype of isolated Cuk converter fed SRM drive is demonstrated here. The obtained input current THD complies with given regulation for harmonics, such as an IEC 61000-3-2.

articleTitle: Design of a Miniaturized Omni-Directional RF-to-dc IR-WPT
abstract: This paper proposes the design and experimental validations of a 13,56 MHz IR-WPT link with a conformal transmitter (Tx) and a miniaturized (about 1 cubic centimeter) receiver (Rx). The Rx is composed of three receiving coils wrapped around a miniaturized sphere and mutually orthogonal, arranged in such a way that quasi-constant dc-output voltage and efficiency are obtained, regardless of the receiver orientation in 3-D. The conformal transmitter is designed to maximize the coupling coefficient, at a reference distance of 5 cm, and is about 7 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>. The quasi-constant output voltage is obtained by connecting each Rx coil to its class-E rectifiers, optimized together with the rest of the system, and by series-connecting their dc output ports, thus de-facto removing any possible dark zone. With a 10-V input source, the dc-output voltage is always above 2.7 V and an average conversion efficiency of 13% for any possible 3-D receiver orientation is obtained.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of EMI Shielding Method using Intermediate Coil for Train WPT System
abstract: In this paper, we proposed an intermediate coil to reduce third harmonic EMI component, which is the highest harmonic EMI component in wireless power transfer (WPT) system. WPT system transfers power wirelessly from Tx coil to Rx coil. When Tx part driving power, unwanted harmonic components are generated from inverter of Tx part and rectifier of Rx part. The proposed intermediate coil can effectively lower third harmonic component without degrading the WPT system efficiency. Three-dimensional electromagnetic simulation and circuit simulation are used to verify the effect of the proposed intermediate coil. Thus, we finally achieved the optimal intermediate coil, which reduce third harmonic component nearly 3 dB with 2% increase in system efficiency.

articleTitle: Omnidirectional inductive wireless charging of a 3D receiver cube inside a box
abstract: Omnidirectional inductive wireless charging of a 6×6×6 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> 3D receiver cube with 6 planar coils inside a 47×47×47 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> box with 4 planar emitting coils is studied. The power delivered to the cube in the central position of the box is in the 1 W-2.4 W range with 6-7% transfer efficiency. In this position, the power is insensitive to the pitch angular orientation. When moving the 3D receiver cube toward the corners of the box, there is no sudden drop of transmitted power. However, the delivered power near the corners increases or decreases in an acceptable range depending on the orientations of the magnetic field of the emitters. Perspectives of this work, when replacing the manufacturing of coils based on PCBs technology by 3D Molded Interconnect Device technology, are briefly discussed.

articleTitle: 900 MHz Miniaturized Rectenna
abstract: This paper addresses the design and the characterization of a new topology of compact rectenna used for electromagnetic energy harvesting of low incident electromagnetic power densities. The rectenna uses a broadband miniaturized flat dipole antenna with a single diode rectifier. The experimental results demonstrate that the efficiency of the proposed compact rectenna is up to 38% at 900MHz for electromagnetic power density of 0.26 μW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Resonance and Distance Insensitive Wireless Power. Transfer with Parity-Time Symmetric Duffing Resonators
abstract: In this paper, a concept of parity-time (PT) symmetry from quantum physics, which enables constantefficiency energy transfer between linear LC resonators within a definite range of transfer distance, is extended to WPT systems with Duffing resonators. By considering nonlinear resonance properties and introducing complex variables, the coupled-mode models of WPT systems with Duffing resonators are derived. Thereafter, transfer performance in the steady state is investigated in an explicit way according to coupled-mode theory (CMT) as well as the parameter conditions of an exact PT symmetric phase. In comparison with PT symmetry-based WPT systems with linear LC resonators, WPT systems with PT symmetric Duffing resonators exhibit combined features of distance and resonance detuning insensitivity. Finally, a system is designed to maintain constant transfer efficiency of 84% with a resonance detuning tolerance of nearly 5%, which is confirmed by simulation results.

articleTitle: High Efficiency Frequency Shift Keying Data Transmission System using Magnetic Resonance Wireless Power Transfer
abstract: This paper describes a high efficiency unidirectional Frequency Shift Keying (FSK) data transmission system using magnetic resonance wireless power transfer (MR-WPT) with the Automatic Tuning Assist Circuit (ATAC) for moving objects. In the proposed system, power and data are transmitted to the same direction at the same time. In the original MR-WPT system with ATAC, when the driving frequency is changed according to data, a certain amount of time is required to shift the other resonant state. This tracking time causes problems such as the decreasing of power transfer efficiency and limitation of data transmission rate. So, in order to overcome these problems, this paper proposes FSK communication system with two ATACs. Since the two ATACs system can reduce the transition time, the MR-WPT with two ATACs can maintain high efficiency power transfer with data. The experimental results show that data transmission by FSK modulation without error can be realized up to 12.5kbps.

articleTitle: Direction-of-Arrival Estimation by Utilizing Harmonic Reradiation from Rectenna
abstract: We propose a new direction-of-arrival (DoA) method for wireless power transfer (WPT) by utilizing harmonic reradiation from rectenna. A feature of the proposed method is needlessness of a pilot signal oscillator in the receiving site, then the receiving system can be configured without any power supplies and batteries. We developed and experimentally investigated the harmonic-reradiated DoA estimation system. We verified that the measurement results were comparable with a conventional DoA estimation and simulation results, except for the interference with the direct incoming waves from the WPT transmitter. We discussed error factors from viewpoints of mutual coupling effects on receiving antennas, and asymmetric property of the receiving antennas including feeding points, as well as the interference with the WPT transmitter. By calibrating the measured data, the harmonic-reradiated DoA estimation errors were mitigated within the range from -2.1° to 3.5°.

articleTitle: Digital Coil: Transmitter Coil with Programmable Radius for Wireless Powering Robust Against Distance Variation
abstract: A wireless powering system robust against distance variation is required. In this paper, a digital transmitter (TX) coil, whose radius depends on the distance (d) between the TX and receiver (RX) coils, is proposed that maximizes the efficiency of wireless powering. Firstly, we analytically derived the optimum TX coil radius (r<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TX, OPT</sub>) to maximize the coil-to-coil efficiency (1) by cooptimizing the coupling coefficient and the quality factors of the coils. It was found that r<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TX, OPT</sub> was approximately equal to d. Then, a practical implementation of the digital TX coil, whose radius was electrically varied without mechanical motion, was proposed. It was found by a measurement that, compared with a conventional TX coil with a constant radius, the proposed digital TX coil increased η from 12% to 20% when d was four times the RX coil radius.

articleTitle: A Novel Method for Online Coupling Factor Determination in Inductive Power Transfer Systems
abstract: The transient behaviour of serially compensated inductive power transfer systems contains overshoots in the current, which have to be taken into account for the overall system dimensioning. In this contribution, a relation between the coupling factor and the transient response of a system is discovered. The overshoot duration and the envelope of the current show a dependence on design frequency and coupling factor only. With this discovery, the coupling factor can be estimated during operation without any additional communication channel or short-circuit measurements. This novel method for online (i. e., during operation) parameter identification is especially of interest for dynamic energy transfer and for systems in which the coupling factor changes over time.

articleTitle: Real-time Optimization of Coil Positioning in Wireless Power Transfer System for Artificial Heart
abstract: An artificial heart system is clinically used for the blood circulation of the heart failure patient. The power of it is supplied via a drive line from the outside of the body. In order to eliminate the drive line from the patient, we propose a wireless poser transfer system with magnetic resonant coupling. The system will be placed inside the room and track the motion of the patient with a receiver coil. According to the information of patient's motion, the position and posture of a movable transmitter coil and a repeater coil are actively controlled in order to keep the high transfer efficiency. In this study, we have developed a real-time calculation algorithm to obtain the optimal coil positions and postures. Then the calculation time and effectiveness of the proposed algorithm were evaluated.

Author Keywords: real-time optimization of coil position and posture

articleTitle: Study on Multipath Retrodirective for Microwave Power Transmission
abstract: In this paper, we verified the effectiveness of multipath retrodirective. We calculated and simulated the phase change of the pilot signal caused by the interference with multipath, and both results agreed. Thus, simulating multipath retrodirective, we clarified that the accuracy of multipath retrodirective is determined by the number of elements and the element interval of the Van atta array. Retrodirectivity became better with the number of antenna elements in multipath environment. The transmission efficiency was degraded by mutual coupling when the element interval was λ/4. When the element interval was λ/2 and antenna elements were increased, the maximum power was able to transmitted. Comparing maximum power in multipath environment to maximum power in free space, we clarified Multipath Retrodirective is more efficient.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Relationship between the Parameters of IPT Transformer and Power Electronic System
abstract: Inductive power transfer (IPT) is a promising technology that can replace the wire based power transfer. Efficiency of these systems will be a critical performance index that will determine their future in commercial applications. This paper analyses a series-series(SS) compensated IPT system using Boucherot bridge current source model to establish the relationship between magnetic pad parameters (mutual inductance) and power electronic system parameters (input and output voltages and currents). Analysis was used to design a 3.7 kW IPT system. The design is validated with the aid of finite element analysis software, ANSYS Maxwell and Simplorer. The proposed design is capable of transferring power at an efficiency of 95.88%. Furthermore, analysis shows that the mutual inductance requirement decreases with the increase in rated power for a SS compensated IPT system.

articleTitle: A Comparison of GaN Class E Inverter and Synchronous Rectifier Designs for 13.56 MHz, 27.12 MHz and 40.68 MHz ISM Bands
abstract: A comparative study of class-E inverter and synchronous rectifier designs is made for wireless power applications operating in the 13.56 MHz, 27.12 MHz and 40.68 MHz frequency bands. All the designs use the same GaN switch, gate driver, and PCB layout to provide a consistent reference for comparing the performance of the different designs. The synchronous rectifier circuits are designed as circuit duals of the inverters using the theory of time reversal duality. A comparison of power efficiency is made for different frequency bands as well as for the inverter and rectifier duals. The results show that the inverter and rectifier duals are well matched in terms of efficiency.

articleTitle: Design of Magnetic Coupling Resonant Wireless Charging System for Cable Tunnel Inspection Robot
abstract: A wireless power transfer system for automatically charging the inspection robot in cable tunnels is proposed in this paper. The design procedure of the magnetic coupling resonant wireless charging system is presented. The ZVS condition of the Class-E inverter, and the constant-current charging function are discussed. Also, an infrared module is added to the control system to detect the alignment of the transmitter and receiver coils so as to automatically switch the operation modes between charging and standby. Experimental results verify that the designed wireless charging system can be operated stably and efficiently.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on Over 10 Meters Magnetic Resonance Wireless Power Transfer under Sea with Coils
abstract: It is difficult to power the object wirelessly under the sea because sea has the property of high conductivity [1]. We study on electromagnetic field in lossy media. We make experiments on magnetic resonance wireless power transfer system with multiple coils which are sunk into sea completely and measure the parameters of coils, coupling coefficient, efficiency and wattage. As a result, we confirm over 10 metric wireless power transfer under sea.

articleTitle: A Capacitive Power Transfer System with a CL Network for Improved System Performance
abstract: This paper introduces the analysis and optimization of capacitive power transfer system with a CL compensation circuit on the secondary for reduced voltage stress across the electric field coupling interface and less system sensitivity. The system has been mathematically analyzed to understand the effect of the CL circuit. And simulation and experimental studies are also carried out for verifications. It is found by increasing C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> (and reducing L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> accordingly to be tuned to the nominal frequency), the quality factor (Q) can be reduced to make the system less sensitive to circuit parameter and load variations, thus easier to tune. However, the CL network should be carefully designed to reduce the voltage stress and electric field leakage around the interface. A practical circuit is built which has demonstrated 5 W of power transfer across a combined interface capacitance of ~1 nF at an operating frequency of 1 MHz, and the system power efficiency is above 65%. The voltage stress and sensitivity reduction have been confirmed practically.

articleTitle: Novel Diplexer-based Harmonic Transponder for 5G-Compatible IoT Applications
abstract: A novel diplexer-based passive harmonic transponder for 5G-compatible IoT applications is presented in this work. Tx/Rx isolation is obtained through the generation of the 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> harmonic signal. The proposed architecture design is based on a high isolation diplexer with a single (dual band) antenna as opposed to a traditional design using two-antenna isolation. Such an architecture relaxes the stringent design requirements of antennas in traditional architectures. Subsequently, antennas with enhanced performance can be utilized without resorting to compromise. Measured results of the proposed transponder circuit have shown improved performance over the state of the art counterparts. The conversion loss is about 20.2 dB at -30 dBm input power, which shows more than 10 dB better than previous work.

articleTitle: Development of 94GHz microstrip line rectenna
abstract: In an RF energy wireless power transfer, it is a strong point to choose a millimeter-wave band. Because the system can be more compact-size caused by shorter wavelength. Then, it is possible to reduce a rectenna area if the rectified DC power is equivalent to a microwave rectenna. This is a great advantage for high power and light weight application like flying vehicles. In this study, a 94 GHz rectenna was developed and evaluated. Before integration, using finline, a rectifier and an antenna were evaluated separately. When load resistance is 125 $\Omega$ at the input power of 104 mW, rectifying efficiency was obtained by 46%. The gain of 16-element microstrip antenna (MSA) was 9.0 dBi. After integration, the rectifying efficiency of rectenna $(\eta_{rec})$ was 27.4% at the input power of 3S.0mW, and the rectenna conversion efficiency $(\eta_{con})$ was 2.75% at the receiving power of 37S mW. The measurement of the rectenna was performed under power condensed condition to increase the input power.

articleTitle: Application of Wireless Power Transfer in Totally Implantable Heart Pump
abstract: The top challenges for widespread application of ventricular assist device are infections of the driveline and pump thrombosis of the device. This project makes use of the powerful multiphysics computational simulation to improve the design of the left ventricular assist devices, by eliminating the driveline and streamlining the pump interior blood contacting surfaces. The design optimization involves balancing the wireless power transfer efficiency, implant miniaturization, and the regulatory compliance.

articleTitle: Load-Independent ZPA Conditions in Both Constant Current and Constant Voltage Modes of LCC-Series Compensated IPT System
abstract: In wireless EV charging application, constant current/constant voltage charging profile is desirable for LithiumIon battery load. In addition, it is not easy for a open-loop IPT system to achieve zero phase angle (ZPA) condition over the entire charge process without any additional control algorithm and auxiliary circuit. In this paper, a design method for the LCC-series compensated inductive power transfer (IPT) system is investigated to obtain not only load-independent current and voltage transfer characteristics but load-independent ZPA operating conditions in both constant current (CC) and constant votlage (CV) modes. A 3.3-kW LCC-series compensated IPT prototype has been implemented to demonstrate the feasibility and validity of the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Ambient RF Energy Harvesting for Dual-Band frequencies below 6 GHz
abstract: In order to boost energy that could be exploited, dual or multi-band channels are needed to scavenge and harvest ambient RF energy. In this paper, a dual-band RF energy harvester is designed to operate in dual-band frequencies below 6 GHz. The signal received is harvested using a Schottky diode HSMS 2850. The circuit is optimized for low input power level using a Harmonic balance simulator. At the design phase, different dual-band frequencies are tested to show the flexibility of the proposed topology. Different methods of impedance matching have been investigated. A variety of Schottky diode implementation have been considered. The design is optimized to cover the two bands around 2.45 and 5.2 GHz. in the measurement, a shift in the dual-band to 1.95-4.8 GHz is observed. The two bands have been setup to measure their output voltage are 2-4.8 GHz. At2 GHz a maximum output voltage measured is 1.970 V at 24 dBm of the input power. For 4.8 GHz, a maximum output measured is 1.784 V at 24 dBm.

articleTitle: Enhanced Planar Wireless Power Transfer Systems with Ferrite Material
abstract: Three ferrite component structures are presented and incorporated into the planar magnetically coupled resonance (MCR) wireless power transfer (WPT) systems in this paper. They are then employed to build two WPT systems which are simulated and tested. The ferrite core and ferrite plate being introduced improve the transmission efficiency by 16.2%. The ferrite plate and ferrite sheet effectively mitigate the magnetic leakage and restore the transmission efficiency when metal object placed in proximity of the receiver. Our results show that the proposed ferrite configurations can benefit the planar WPT systems for small electronic devices.

articleTitle: Harnessing Magneto-inductive Waves for Wireless Power Transfer
abstract: Magneto-inductive waves (MIWs) - waves of inter-element excitation in ensembles of resonant electric circuits can carry power and signals across surfaces in metamaterial-based devices. The propagation of MIWs is governed by both the dispersion of the supporting metamaterial, its geometry and the presence of lattice defects. Here, we demonstrate how by introducing defects in a two-dimensional (2D) MIW-supporting metamaterial we can control the propagation of MIWs. This principle is used for advanced wireless power-transfer devices: power can be directed to specific areas of 2D surfaces via defect ensembles with pre-designed interference with MIWs or quasi-1D power-transfer channels.

articleTitle: Capacitive Power Transfer based on Compensation Circuit for Class E Resonant Full-Wave Rectifier

authors.preferredName: Susanna Vital de Campos de Freitas

abstract: This paper outlines, for the first time, the use of a class E resonant full-wave rectifier in a capacitive power transfer (CPT) system, working at megahertz (MHz) in the medium power range. In order to cancel the reactances introduced by the rectifier and coupling capacitors, equations to determine the required compensation inductors are derived based on circuit analysis. Measurements of input impedance, output power, and system's efficiency are presented and verified by simulations.

articleTitle: Harmonic-recycling Rectifier Design for Localization and Power Tuning
abstract: This work introduces a new rectifier for wireless power transfer (WPT) with harmonic-recycling capability for enhanced functionality beyond RF-DC conversion. By taking advantages of nonlinearity of the diode, in the proposed rectifier circuits, the second harmonic is utilized for communication with the transmitter. It can be used as a feedback signal to the transmitter to (1) control the transmitting beam direction for maximum efficiency and (2) to determine the status of the attached load, whether the load is turned on. With the design of a multi-functional rectifier, it is possible to realize a close-loop system to achieve efficient WPT.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study of a Wireless Power Transfer System Applied to a Leadless Pacemaker
abstract: This study deals with the battery recharge of a leadless pacemaker, which has been recently introduced in the market, by means of the wireless power transfer (WPT) technology based on the magnetic resonant coupling. The main difficulty is given by the depth of the leadless pacemaker implantation inside the human body. The electromagnetic problem mainly consists in the selection of the on-body excitation (primary coil current and frequency), which must adequately energize the leadless pacemaker without any exceedance of the basic restrictions (BRs) specified by the electromagnetic field (EMF) safety standards. Another relevant problem consists in the weight of the leadless pacemaker within the secondary coil that must be very light. In this paper, a feasibility study is carried out to define possible solutions for this kind of application.

articleTitle: Dynamic Complex Impedance Tuning Method Using a Multiple-Input DC/DC Converter for Wireless Power Transfer
abstract: The performance of a wireless power transfer (WPT) system is highly dependent on the complex impedance of the receiver (RX). Therefore, dynamic complex impedance tuning methods are critical pieces for gaining sufficient control over WPT systems. However, prior methods cannot achieve the following three requirements simultaneously: high-frequency $(i.e.\ \mathrm{MHz},\ \mathrm{GHz})$ operation, continuous complex impedance tuning, and few additional components. To overcome these challenges, we present a dynamic complex impedance tuning method based on multiple-input $\mathrm{D}\mathrm{C}/\mathrm{D}\mathrm{C}$ converters andLC filters. The active operations used in our method are closed in the low-frequency (i.e. after-rectification) region of the circuit; it has the promise of achieving the three above-mentioned requirements. The proposed method was evaluated through theoretical analysis and SPICE simulations assuming a 6.78 MHz near-field WPT system. It was shown that the complex impedance can be tuned in a wide range in the complex plane; by using our method, the fluctuation of power factor can be suppressed to 1%, whereas prior methods show 12%.

articleTitle: Varactor-based Rectifier with Adaptive Matching Network for Wireless Power Transfer system
abstract: This work presents an adaptive matching network for rectifier circuit in wireless power transfer system by using varactor diode. By setting appropriate biasing voltages, the changes in the capacitances of the varactor enable the rectifier to reconfigure in response to the fluctuations in operating conditions, such as input power level and frequency. This allows the system to remain efficient despite changes in the external factors. Furthermore, integration with microcontroller unit (MCU) is without consuming excessive power. This would allow the rectifier circuit to become optimizable in real time.

articleTitle: A Wireless Power Transfer System for MRI Scanners
abstract: Wireless power transfer is a key component to creating comfortable and completely wireless MRI receive coil arrays. Here, a WPT system is presented using a Class-E power amplifier driving an array of primary coils with a single secondary coil and Class-E rectifier. An RF MEMs switched adjustable impedance matching system is added to match the variable load presented by the coupled coils to the desired load of the power amplifier. The system is shown to be capable of transferring several watts of power inside the MRI bore.

articleTitle: Wideband Rectenna with Inductive High-Impedance Folded Dipole Antenna
abstract: For wideband conjugate matching, the inductive high-impedance folded dipole antenna is proposed to be combined with a rectifier with capacitive admittance, in this paper. The proposed rectenna achieves relative bandwidth of 43%, which covers the entire Japanese DTV bandwidth (470-700 MHz). The measured rectification efficiency is higher than 19% at the input power of -15 dBm.

articleTitle: Comparison of active and passive sensors for IoT applications
abstract: The concept behind Internet of Things (IoT) has been widely addressed in the last years. Developments in many field facilitate the emergence of multiple approaches to develop Wireless Sensor Networks (WSN). This paper presents a comparison between a passive and active solution for a short-rage WSN. The work compares different approaches to create a WSN based on commercial technologies (Bluetooth) and a custom solution that utilizes Wireless Power Transmission (WPT) and backscatter. The waste explores the architectures power consumption, the battery production and efficiency process.

articleTitle: Influence of the Titanium Case used in Implantable Medical Devices on the Wireless Power Link
abstract: Titanium cases are usually used as the main enclosure of implantable medical devices (IMDs), such as pacemaker. Different titanium alloys with different resistivities exist. Currently, the wireless powering of such IMDs is a challenging research topic. In this work, the influence that different titanium alloys have on the wireless power transfer link is studied at 13.56 MHz. It is shown in simulations and measurements, that a worst resistivity for the case of the implantable medical device exists, which minimizes the link efficiency. A simplified analytical model is also presented to understand this effect. Additionally, we show that titanium grade 2, which has a lower resistivity (better conductor) than titanium grade 5, achieves higher link efficiency than the grade 5, in our design at 13.56 MHz. Therefore, this analysis proves that the titanium alloy electrical characteristics should be carefully considered in the design of the wireless power transfer link.

articleTitle: A Sourceless Low-Power mmW Receiver Architecture Using Self-Oscillating Mixer Array in 65-nm CMOS
abstract: In this paper, a CMOS sourceless millimeter-wave receiver for next generation wireless communication and sensing systems including 5G is proposed and demonstrated. It makes use of injection-locked self-oscillating mixers, in order to enable a direct-conversion to baseband without any external LO nor an IF block, therefore greatly reducing power consumption. This architecture is created through multi-input and multi-output arrays in connection with slicing frequency spectrum or frequency band of interest. In this way, the proposed receiver supports a high transmission throughoutput based on frequency-diversified multiple inputs/outputs, which presents a unique feature in the implementation of a low-power and high bit-rate communication system.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis Applying the AMSL Method to Predict the Magnetic Field in an EV with a WPT System
abstract: A recently developed method, named as artificial material single layer (AMSL), is applied to predict the magnetic field distributions inside and outside an electric vehicle (EV) equipped with a wireless power transfer (WPT) technology. The AMSL method is very efficient to predict field reflection and transmission of conductive layers as EV bodyshell and it considerably reduces the computational cost compared to conventional Finite Element Method (FEM) an analysis. Some test cases are examined to illustrate the implementation of the AMSL method for WPT automotive applications. The obtained results demonstrate the accuracy of the method.

articleTitle: Exploiting Nonlinearity to Design Robust Wireless Power Transfer and Wideband RF Energy Harvesting
abstract: In this paper, the design of position-insensitive wireless power transfer (WPT) circuits and wideband RF wireless energy harvesting (WEH) circuits are presented. The unique properties of a specific class of nonlinear resonant circuits described by a 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> order nonlinear differential equation with cubic or higher order nonlinear terms are exploited to design such circuits.The position-insensitive WPT circuit maintains a high power transmission efficiency (PTE) over large transmission distance and misalignment variations without tuning the source's operating frequency or employing tunable matching networks and active feedback/control circuitry. The wideband WEH circuit utilizes a nonlinear resonant circuit to significantly enhance its bandwidth. Both a WPT and a WEH circuit have been designed and tested. The WPT circuit achieves a constant power transfer and PTE of 20 W and 85%, respectively, over a varying transmission distance of 250 mm. On the other hand, the WEH circuit using a nonlinear resonator achieves 2.7 times bandwidth enhancement as compared to a similar circuit employing a linear resonator having the same quality factor,Q.

articleTitle: Basic Study for Wireless Power Transfer to a Pipeline Inspection Robot
abstract: Our goal is to transfer power to a pipeline inspection robot by using microwave. We calculated cutoff frequencies and attenuation coefficients of each propagation mode by electromagnetic theory of a waveguide, since a gas pipeline can be regarded as a circular waveguide. We simulated a joint part of pipes, and found that the loss caused by a joint part is much smaller than the attenuation of the microwave. We conducted simulations on curved pipes as well and clarified how propagation modes convert at curved pipes.

articleTitle: Robust Active Tuning for Wireless Power Transfer to Support Misalignments and Variable Load
abstract: Wireless power transfer has been employed in several applications where the use of cables for powering remote devices are not suitable or feasible. However, such devices work in a tuned frequency and thus the transferred power is set to make the system operate under resonant conditions. These conditions and, in turn the transferred power, are highly dependent on the parameters of an equivalent electrical circuit. Such power can drop abruptly with variations of the relative position between the transmitter and receiver coils as well as the variations of the output load. This work presents a multi-variable with method for maximizing the output power in a wireless power transfer system to make it robust to misalignments and load variations. The described method monitors the magnitude and phase of the input current of the inductive link and proposes an automatic control algorithm by controlling both, the source frequency and a variable matching network. Preliminary results showed that the power delivered to the load can be hold approximately constant over a large range of magnetic coupling coefficient and the load values. These results are a significant improvement of the results obtained by controlling only the source frequency or only the matching network.

articleTitle: A Wideband Cascaded Skew Planar Wheel Antenna for RF Energy Harvesting
abstract: This paper presents the design and measurement of a novel cascaded skew planar wheel (SPW) antenna that harvests radio frequency (RF) energy from ambient Wi-Fi to energize a low power temperature sensor. The proposed novel circularly polarized quasi-isotropic antenna incorporates two cascaded SPW antennas of varying scale, spaced apart by $\lambda /8$. This design results in a simulated gain of 4.76 dB, a 1.1 dB increase from the conventional skew planar antenna, and a 35% increase in the measured -10 dB bandwidth. The antenna was then integrated into an Internet of Things (IoT) system to power a temperature sensor. Using the cascaded SPW in the system significantly improves the DC voltage generated at the output of the charge pump by up to 60% depending on the input RF power received.

articleTitle: Design of Transmitter Coil Antennas for Inductive Resonant Power Transfer
abstract: As people want to remove cables from their mobile devices, wireless charging becomes more and more important. Out of the different wireless power transfer (WPT) schemes, resonant inductive coupled WPT offers high transmission efficiencies paired with high spatial freedom in the position of the receiver and is thus of special interest in consumer electronics. To achieve high transmission efficiencies while allowing high spatial freedom, the transmitter coil of an inductively coupled WPT system has to be optimized. Here, we investigate the design of a printed-circuit-board (PCB) transmitter coil and consider skin effect, current crowding and proximity effect to optimize our design for a frequency of 6.78 MHz. In the end, we validate our theoretical model by comparing the predicted losses with the real losses in a WPT system resulting in a deviation of 10 % between model and measurement of a manufactured coil.

articleTitle: Contactless Power Transfer Using Capacitive Resonant Single-Conductor Structure

authors.preferredName: Susanna Vital de Campos de Freitas

abstract: While single-conductor power transfer (SCPT) technology presents low losses and mitigates the issues of misalignment in inductive (IPT) and capacitive power transfer (CPT), it still requires a physical connection between transmitter and receiver by means of a wire. This paper presents the addition of a discontinuity in the SCPT in the form of one pair of capacitive plates, providing contactless power delivery, which represents an improvement when compared to the two pairs of capacitive plates required in regular CPT. In addition, this paper introduces the concept that the entire single-conductor structure, the resonators and the coils must resonate collectively. Measurement results are presented to analyze the efficiency and input impedance behavior versus frequency. Finally, it is demonstrated that the developed SCPT system achieves an efficiency of 72% at 6.78 MHz, with a 3 cm gap between the capacitive plates.

articleTitle: Two-tone FSK Modulation for SWIPT
abstract: We propose a two-tone Frequency Shift Keying (FSK) modulation scheme that is suited for simultaneous efficient wireless power transfer and data transfer (SWIPT), by exploiting non-linearities of the rectifier. The result is a spectrum and hardware efficient solution: data and energy are jointly transmitted in the air, and are received by the same hardware. We elaborate on a Fourier transformation-based non-coherent FSK receiver for the proposed scheme and show the theoretical relation between throughput and bandwidth. We demonstrate the trade-off between information and power transfer efficiency for the proposed two-tone FSK modulation scheme. This is also confirmed by measurement results which shows data transfer at 7 Mbps in a more efficient power transfer operating region than demonstrated in the current state of the art.

articleTitle: Wireless Power Transfer with Multi-Layer Planar Spiral Coils as Secondary Coils
abstract: As the sizes of implantable medical devices such as implantable cardioverter defibrillators, deep brain stimulators, and retinal implants shrink; powering these devices become more challenging. Wireless power transfer (WPT) enables the use of rechargeable and thus smaller batteries, however it also requires additional space for the receiving coil. Depending on the location of the implant in the body, device area or volume can be more constrained. In this paper, we investigate multi-layer planar spiral coils via simulations. We study the impact of number of turns on the quality factor for multi-layer coils including coils with different number of turns in each layer (hybrid coils) and we offer recommendations on the approximate number of turns for having high Q values.

articleTitle: A Novel Contactless Capacitive Energy and Data Transfer System
abstract: This article presents a novel contactless capacitive energy and data transfer system. The system is used to supply and communicate with low power devices especially for applications with limited space. A typical use case are sensors in electrical machines or in gearboxes. Regarding this, commonly used inductive data and energy transfer systems are spatially too large. Basis of the work is an auto-resonant power oscillator, commonly called royer converter, which provides a frequency shift key modulation by changing the capacitance of its own resonant circuit. To evaluate the novel data transfer, the system is set up and some measurements are presented to show the satisfactory result.

articleTitle: Multi-Stage Schottky Diode Power Harvester for UWB application
abstract: This paper presents a broadband high sensitive RF power harvester for UWB and multi-band applications. Schottky diodes are traditionally used for their low threshold voltage, which increases the efficiency of low power RF-DC conversion. The usual diode-based design is suitable only for narrowband applications. The proposed distributed RF harvester used a periodic structure which looks like an artificial transmission line (TL) structure. It has been demonstrated that an arrangement of five-stage distributed converter and TLs with characteristic impedance of 200 to replace inductance can operates from very low frequencies up to 11 GHz. The distributed harvester has a significant improvement in the detected voltage over a wide bandwidth compared to conventional RF detectors. The obtained bandwidth was better than 10 GHz (166%) at center frequency of 6 GHz ranging from (1-11) GHz. Peak Efficiency is varying from 20% to 80% over this band. A minimum voltage sensitivity of 40 pV and the peak value more 1.7 V are reached at 6 GHz.

articleTitle: Exact Statistical Characterization of RF-Energy Harvesting over Rice Fading Channel
abstract: RF-energy harvesting has been one of the hottest research topics in wireless communications for the past few years. It found applications in cognitive radio networks, wireless sensor networks, personal area networks, device-to-device communications and a host of other wireless technologies. However, fundamental characteristics of the RF-energy harvesting process have been widely overlooked, often for mathematical convenience. These are i) the harvested energy is a statistical process, ii) the harvesting circuit has a sensitivity level that has to be met for harvesting to happen. In [1], we have shown that the amount of harvested energy is a linear function of the amount of incident energy, which can be statistically modeled using the Sampling Theorem. In this article, we capitalize on that result and derive the statistical characteristics of the harvested energy over a sequence of N harvesting blocks. The findings of this article give researchers a useful mathematical tool to design realistic RF-energy harvesting protocols.

articleTitle: Capacitively Coupled Resonator Models for Investigating Spatial Impedance Variation in WPT Systems
abstract: An analysis of a capacitive wireless power transfer system is presented to investigate the relationship between spatial impedance variation between the transmitter and receiver. The capacitively coupled link is modeled by an equivalent circuit that includes all coupling paths between the four conductors which make up the link. The analysis shows that a low Q resonator circuit is desirable to minimize impedance changes from spatial variation. On the other hand, the presence of crosslink capacitances can increase the Q which can be obtained after matching the circuit. Therefore cross-link capacitances should be minimized for spatially robust systems. Experimental results for ISM band frequencies of 13.56 MHz, 27.12 MHz, and 40.68 MHz are shown to verify the analysis.

articleTitle: Power Loss Analysis of Inverter with and without Transformer for Capacitive Power Transfer
abstract: This paper investigates the power loss characteristics in the circuit for the capacitive power transfer (CPT) system using analog circuit simulation focusing on the high voltage pulse generator with and without step-up transformer. The CPT usually has low capacitance value in their coupled capacitance due to the physical dimension and low dielectric constant of the interface, hence the high voltage with high-frequency switching needed to transfer the power through it. Using a simple LC resonant circuit and 1 MHz frequency operation, the power losses in inverter MOSFETs and transformer are analyzed under the condition with output power of 200W at 200Ω load resistance. The simulation results indicate that the inverter with step-up transformer with lower series resistance in both of wire strands can decrease the losses at MOSFETs with better efficiency compared to the high DC voltage supplied inverter without step-up transformer.

articleTitle: Radio Frequency Power Source Design for Wireless Power Transfer System
abstract: In this paper, a novel design of a radio frequency power source for a wireless power transfer (WPT) system using magnetic coupled resonances (MCR) is described, prototyped and tested. The fabrication of the prototype and test results demonstrate that the design allows for both a high frequency power source and a more compact structure than has previously been demonstrated for MCR-based WPT systems, and thereby advances the potential applicability of such systems.

articleTitle: A High Frequency Data Transmission Method for Contactless Energy Transfer Systems
abstract: Wireless charging systems commonly use far field communication for the charge process control and authentication. This paper presents a near field communication method which is easily integrable to series-series compensated contactless energy transfer (CET) systems. This method is based on shared use of the CET coupled coils for energy transfer and high frequency communication in the range of 7 to 10 MHz. A verification with an experimental prototype was done. Using an orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) modulation allows data rates of approximately 2 Mbit/s and a low bit error rate. This makes the technique suitable for communication during a contactless charging process.

articleTitle: Smart Multi-Coil-based Magnetic Resonance Prototype for Wireless Power Transfer
abstract: Magnetic resonance is a promising technique of far-field wireless power transfer for consumer electronic devices due to its high efficiency and long charging distance. In this paper, we present a smart multi-coil array magnetic resonance charging prototype which can integrate several intelligent functions and charge multiple devices simultaneously with high efficiency. In this platform, magnetic beamforming, impedance matching network and receiver position estimation are implemented on this platform. With these schemes, the received power and transfer efficiency are increased effectively. The experimental results indicate that our platform can effectively charge a device in 20cm with above 90% transmission efficiency.

articleTitle: “Grand Bassin” Case Study: An Original Proof-Of-Concept Prototype for Wireless Power Transportation
abstract: This article presents the synthesis of results to the case study that was carried out to the Reunion Island in 2001 on a Wireless Power Transportation (WPT) system. The objective was to demonstrate the feasibility of a point-to-point link transferring energy via a 2.45 GHz microwave beam to a small isolated mountain village (Grand-Bassin). The distance between the reception system and the emitter source was 700m. The emitter antenna was composed of an array of magnetron/reflector. The rectifying element in reception used an original wire antenna while integrated well in the natural environment and presented good performances. To validate this study, a WPT prototype has been built and publicly demonstrated in La Reunion. This prototype has exhibited an overall power transfer efficiency of 6 % from the main electricity grid to the load.

articleTitle: Demonstration of a high-efficiency MWPT System for Aerospace
abstract: Microwave wireless power transmission (MWPT) has wide application in aerospace, especially at the Space Solar Power Station (SSPS), and Payload Spacecraft Module, and high power weapon, and so on. As a new-style transmission mode, MWPT could solve the limitation of electric power in space application. Based on the theory analysis, the MWPT system design scheme is described. The key technologies of MWPT are analyzed, and the demonstration system has been designed and the corresponding measurement results are provided. The experimental results could agree with the target. The power transmission distance is 11m, the transmitting power is 50W, and the DC power to DC power transmission efficiency is better than 16.5%. The research could lay the foundation of MWPT technique for space application.

articleTitle: Coil Geometry Optimization for Wireless Power Delivery to Moving Receivers
abstract: Wireless power transfer systems have conventionally been modeled and optimized in static configurations, with immobile receivers and transmitters. However, many real-world use cases are not well addressed by this simplified model. In this work, the case of a moving receiver is explored, and transmit coil geometry is optimized for this special case. The optimal design is based on the velocity of the receiver, energy required by the load, Tx-Rx distance, and maximum receiver size. Simplified equations and design procedures are described and analyzed. Coils and receiver hardware are implemented and validate the design. The Tx-Rx ratio of the implemented coil system is 10.8:1 with a 4.5cm receiver coil.

articleTitle: Antenna Polarization Alignment Using Intermodulation for Multi-Sine Wireless Power Transfer
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: inductive power transmission; coils; microwave power transmission; rectifiers; rectennas; energy harvesting; rectifying circuits; radiofrequency power transmission; DC-DC power convertors; resonators.

articleTitle: Comparator With Self Controlled Delay for Active Rectifiers in Inductive Powering
abstract: In active rectifiers the diodes are replaced by transistors whose gates are controlled by a comparator. The power consumption of these comparators mainly depends on its bias current and working frequency and is not directly scaled with the output power. Therefore, to achieve high efficiency at light loads, the comparator power consumption should be addressed. In this paper, an active rectifier with an output power of 1.37 mW was designed and simulated in a 130nm CMOS technology achieving an efficiency of 95.7%. Each comparator consumes only 3.7 μW and has a feedback loop that automatically compensates the comparator delay in both edges.

articleTitle: Millimeter Wave Agile Transmitter for IoT Operations
abstract: Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) technology has been gathering a large interest in the last decade due to its increasing efficiency. Starting from low-frequency systems via magnetic coupling, the trend has been evolving toward high-frequency solutions, with a particular attention to the emerging 5G wireless communication equipment for the internet of things (IoT). In this respect, WPT has to face new challenges to become competitive at frequencies that will be of utmost importance in the near future, like the 28 GHz band. In this paper, we offer a rigorous combined electromagnetic/nonlinear circuit approach to evaluate the performance of a novel WPT system combining state-of-the-art time-modulated array (TMA) technology and high-performance metal-insulator-metal (MIM) diodes with fast switching time. Merging the advantages of TMAs with MIMs gives rise to a new family of low-power WPT devices, able to efficiently supply energy to the electronics used in IoT networks.

articleTitle: A Simple Reconfigurable Planar Array for MCR-WPT System
abstract: This paper presents a novel reconfigurable array for magnatically-coupled resonant wireless power transfer (R-MCRWPT) system. In this system, the transmitter includes three connected resonant element modules, and the receiver includes two connected element modules. It allows both the transmitting and receiving arrays to be reconfigurable in shapes and positions for the best performance. Unlike the conventional system, the reconfigurability of the proposed system is achieved without any control circuits and changes of resonant and matching capacitances. A prototype was developed and tested. Within the coverage range, the proposed system achieves the power transfer efficiency above 80%. Thus, the proposed system presents a good and simple technique for practical wireless power transfer applications.

articleTitle: Implementation of High Efficiency Coupling Coil in Wireless Power Transfer System
abstract: Generally, a four coil topology is implemented in a resonance wireless power transfer system. This paper investigates the relationship of the impedance, efficiency, transfer distance and mutual inductance in the four coil design. A design procedure is proposed to implement the four coil geometry parameters. To verify the design coil parameters, a four coils are accomplished in this work. The measurement shows the maximum efficiency achieves 92.9% in a coupling distance of 6.5cm.

articleTitle: 2.45-GHz Intermittent Wireless Power Transmission System for Batteryless LED Cosmetic Accessories
abstract: An intermittent wireless power transmission system that enables the supply of power to ultra-small wearable devices from a long distance while maintaining a constant average power has been developed. Intermittent power transmission, in which the transmission peak power becomes large in proportion to the reciprocal of the duty cycle, makes it possible to increase the distance between the transmitter and the receiver. A rhythm detection circuit generates a rhythm signal from the electrical musical signal, and that signal is used as a power-switch control signal for intermittent operation. We fabricated a 2.45-GHz wireless power transmission system that consists of a transmitter and LED false eyelashes; in this arrangement an LED with an ultra-small rectenna is embedded in a false eyelash. The transmitter has an intermittent power control circuit and a patch array antenna with a director antenna whose antenna gain is 13.83 dBi. When the transmitter radiated the power intermittently with a duty cycle of 10% and an average power of 1 W, the LEDs of the false eyelashes flashed in time to the music of a CD at a distance of 1.3 m.

articleTitle: Rectifiers Based on Quadrature Hybrid Coupler with Improved Performance for Energy Harvesting
abstract: This paper presents a method for enhancing RF-dc conversion efficiency of the rectifier based on inkjet-printed quadrature based hybrid coupler (QHC) for wireless energy transfer systems. The input matching network and output load of the rectifier are optimized for optimal RF-dc conversion efficiency. Improvement of about 16 dB input power range is achieved for RF-dc conversion efficiency of 60%. The simulated efficiencies of the rectifiers with and without coupler for 3 MHz LTE signals and output power spectra densities at 1.5 GHz are illustrated.

articleTitle: A Simple and Effective Synchronization Technique for Wireless Power Transfer System
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) systems with dual active bridges have been proposed for conduction loss reduction, bi-directional power transfer and efficiency improvement. However, the synchronization of the system is still a challenge due to the high operating frequency. It is found that the synchronization problem can be decomposed into two parts: frequency locking and zero phase point tracking. In this paper, the voltage across secondary compensation capacitor is utilized for frequency locking, and the output dc voltage for zero phase point tracking. The proposed method is effective and easy to implement, whereas the cost is low due to the simple realization. It works well at high frequency and can withstand large variations of input voltage, load and mutual inductance. The validity is proved by the experiments.

articleTitle: Low Power On/Off Control Method for Active-Diode Applied in Wireless Power Transmission
abstract: In this paper, multiple-pulse (MP) problem of comparator based active rectifier is theoretically analyzed by establishing control loop model. Two methods to eliminate the MP problem are demonstrated. Then a delay time based high precision on/off control method is proposed. The new controller senses the current passing through MOSFET and generates the gate driving signals to control the next operating cycle of the active rectifier. Under a 13.65 MHz wireless power transmission test platform, with the same rectification parameters, the experimental results show that the quiescent power consumption of the proposed controller is reduced by 2/3 compared with that of the comparator-based structure. The reverse current is almost eliminated because the on/off control precision reachesps level. Thus, the conversion efficiency of the rectifier is improved significantly. The good performance of the proposed design shows its well practicality for energy harvesting systems.

articleTitle: Achieving Electromagnetic Compatibility of WPT Antennas for Medical Imaging in MRI
abstract: The compatibility of TX and RX antennas commonly used for WPT is analyzed for use in Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) systems. The analysis revealed that commercially available antennas are not compatible with MRI systems and pose a safety risk to patients. This paper presents a protection circuit that protects the antennas and prevents them from interacting with the MR System. The effectiveness of the circuit is proven through experiments in the MRI system and on the bench. The paper discusses a circuit that can render the WPT coils invisible to the MRI system. The WPT power transfer remained unaffected with this filter circuit. With and without the filter, a maximum power of 22 W was measured at the load with a transfer efficiency of 62%.

articleTitle: Core-Shared-Repeater (CSR) Coil Scheme for Low EMI and Efficient WPT System in Ultra-Thin Digital TV
abstract: In this paper, we propose and analyze an ultra-thin digital TV wireless power transfer (WPT) system. We suggest core-shared-repeater (CSR) coils to get higher performance in terms of coil to coil wireless power transfer efficiency (PTE) and lower electromagnetic interference (EMI). However, it is difficult to achieve higher PTE and lower EMI level due to 50 cm long air-gap, low operating frequency, and compact size of the transmitter (Tx) and receiver (Rx) structures. Therefore, we have proposed two core-shared-repeater (CSR) coils, which are placed on a ferrite core of the Tx coil. The CSR coils are used to confine the leakage magnetic flux from the Tx and transfer to the Rx coils. Furthermore, two CSR coils can be utilized to reduce the 3rd current harmonic by applying a resonant frequency of the CSR coils slightly smaller than three times of operating frequency. Using the proposed WPT system, we improved the coil to coil PTE from 61.8% to 83.9% and reduced the 3rd Rx current harmonic by 19.16 dB scale.

articleTitle: Experimental research and design of microwave power transmission system for SSPS application
abstract: Microwave power transmission (MPT) is the core technology of the Space Solar Power Satellite (SSPS). Experimental research and design of a MPT system considering the proposed limit for the center-of-beam power densities to assure environmental health and safety for microwave transmission was presented in this paper. Under the power density limit, an experimental system with solid power amplifier at 5.8 GHz was constructed and tested. In addition, to solve the problem of efficiency decline because of impedance mismatch in different interface between antenna output and rectifier circuit input, meanwhile to block harmonic re-radiation caused by nonlinearity of rectifier circuit, rectifying surface was researched based on sub-wavelength element in rectenna. By changing structure conjugated match between antenna output impedance and rectifier circuit input impedance, the rectifying surface exhibits a strong restrain to high-order harmonics and eliminating the need for RF filter which is an important element for the traditional rectenna, so the circuit structure is simple and high conversion efficiency can realize. In experiment, the measured maximum conversion efficiency of RF to DC is 57.7 %. The results show that the designed microwave power transmission system is benefit for ground demonstration testing in miniature version and building of SSPS in future.

articleTitle: An Electromagnetic Induced Transparency-like Scheme for Wireless Power Transfer in Contained Aqueous Solutions
abstract: The strong coupling between two ultra high dielectric constant resonators and a contained aqueous solution results in an electromagnetic induced transparency like window that is exploited to efficiently transfer power wirelessly over a distance slightly less than the resonant wavelength inside the solution. The strong coupling allows the scheme to tolerate the intrinsic conducting losses inevitably present in aqueous solutions. In fact, it is shown that the stronger the coupling, the higher the loss tangent that can be tolerated.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Comparison of Impedance Matching Circuits for Inductively Coupled WPT
abstract: In mass production, the deviation of electronic components is inevitable under the cost limitation and fabrication error. The power transfer efficiency (PTE) variation under the deviation of capacitances in the impedance matching circuits (IMCs) of wireless power transfer systems is analyzed in this paper. Although the IMCs corresponding to realizing conjugate impedance matching reach the best PTE, the variation of PTE is larger than the results of basic IMCs in which only one capacitor is used in the receiver side.

articleTitle: A Novel Rectenna Array with RBR for Long-Distance WLAN Energy Harvesting System
abstract: In this paper, a radio frequency (RF) energy harvester by using a rectenna array and rectifier-booster regulators (RBR) is presented. The design focuses on long distance RF energy harvesting. The proposed RBR, which evolves from a Greinacher rectifier and a Dickson charge pump, is implemented to improve the output voltage level of each rectenna. Eachrectenna element is cascaded to an RBR to rectify AC power into to DC and boost the output voltage. The array elements are connected in series to further improve the output voltage. Measurement results indicate that the proposed RF energy harvester can provide over1 V output voltage within a distance of 1 m from a transmit antenna with 20 dBm transmitting power. The harvested energy by the proposed harvester from a WiFi router can be utilized to power internet of thing (IoT) sensor nodes directly. The design has demonstrated the practicability of the proposed harvester in real applications.

articleTitle: Harvesting for Scattering RF-Signals receivable by Mobile Telephones
abstract: This work studies RF energy harvesting as a power supply for wireless (back-)scattering technology in the 2.4 GHz ISM Band. The scattering is accomplished by modulating an incident continuous wave signal (CW) according to an intermediate signal such that the modulated signal is receivable by a Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) receiver. The intermediate signal provides for frequency shifting as well as information carrying modulation and is specifically designed as a signal with a relative low frequency of ca. 4 MHz, which allows for signal generation by a low energy microcontroller. The microcontroller receives its operational energy from a harvesting circuit, which accumulates and intermediately stores the energy of the incident CW signal.
