We achieved unidirectional BLE advertising by combining scattering technology and energy harvesting and thus showed the feasibility of wireless communication from a battery-less RF scattering transponder to a regular mobile telephone.

articleTitle: A Novel Receiver for Dual-side Controlled Wireless Power Transfer System
abstract: Recently, dual-side phase control (PC) is introduced to regulate the output power and track the maximum efficiency of the wireless power transfer system (WPT). Since an active receiver is utilized on the secondary side, the control is complex in nature. In addition, short through may occur and the reliability of the system cannot be guaranteed. In this paper, a novel one-switch receiver is proposed for the dual-side controlled WPT system. The proposed receiver can take full advantage of low switching losses of silicon carbon (SiC) metal-oxide-semiconductor field effect transistor (MOSFET), whereas avoid its high forward voltage loss without paralleling any freewheeling diode. In addition, the proposed receiver advances in easy design and realization, cost effective, free from short through and small size. Experiments are added to verify the proposed plan.

articleTitle: Wideband Monopolar Transmitting Antenna for Wireless Power Transfer and Communication Application
abstract: A proximity-fed circular patch antenna with linear polarization and monopole-like radiation pattern is presented. The antenna achieves a bandwidth (|S11|<; -10 dB) of 50.4% (4.15-6.95 GHz) at the central frequency of 5.55 GHz. The microwave power transmission (MPT) band (5.8GHz) and space shuttle communication band (4.60GHz) can be completely covered. The broadband performance is achieved by exciting multimodes (TM01 and TM02) in the patch. Three resonant points can be observed in the S-parameter curve. The measured minimum and maximum gains in the whole band are 5.1 dBi and 9.4 dBi, respectively. The simulated results and the measured ones are in good agreement. The antenna is pretty suitable for microwave power and information transmission in space shuttle.

articleTitle: Microwave Oven Field Detector Probe
abstract: This article proposes a probe to monitor the electromagnetic field inside microwave ovens. Although magnetrons are now small and highly efficient, and solid state ovens can control the power delivered to the food, neither can `see' the electromagnetic field inside the microwave oven. Therefore, this article proposes a field detector probe, based on a rectenna design, which consists of an antenna and a rectifier, converting the RF signal, inside the cavity, to a DC voltage. The rectifier is based on a LDMOS power transistor (BLC2425M8LS300P) provided by Ampleon. The electromagnetic field inside the microwave oven can be detected and measured by reading the output DC voltage generated by the field detector probe.

articleTitle: Compact C-band Rectenna for Satellite Applications
abstract: This paper addresses the design and the characterization of a compact C-band rectenna for satellite applications. The proposed flat dipole rectenna achieves an efficiency of 58.2% at 3.25 GHz when illuminated with an electromagnetic power density of only 33.9 μW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The proposed rectenna is also compact; its size is 1334 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> that is only 16% of the square wavelength at 3.25 GHz.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Induced Electric Field in Human Body by Wireless Power Transfer System for EV/PHV
abstract: In recent years, research on wireless power transfer system for charging EV / PHV has been developed. For human health protection, it is necessary to pay attention to exposure of human body to the leaked magnetic field from this system. In this paper, the induced electric fields were evaluated for different gap lengths between the primary coil and the secondary coil using electromagnetic field simulation. The computational results show that the induced electric field decreased as the gap length increased.

articleTitle: I/Q Multiport Sensing Feasibility on Ambient Wireless Energy
abstract: This paper presents a multiport sensing system composed of a multiport sensor node and an I/Q multiport receiver. The sensor node comprises a sensor under test and a reference. It is fed by a 100 KHz data rate BPSK signal. The change in reflections that occurs in the sensor (I path) modulates the envelope of the BPSK signal. The receiver is based on a six-port direct demodulator where the I/Q components are obtained using the differential approach to the detected power at the four outputs of the six-port. The real-time measurement results of the demodulated I/Q components give the magnitude and phase variation (sensing) of the sensor in relation to the reference. These results establish the feasibility of using ambient wireless RF energy such as: TV, cellular, and Wi-Fi transmissions in passive sensing. Thus, we avoid overcrowding the available spectrum and facing the expensive process of generating radio waves.

articleTitle: Random Beamforming for Multi-Coil Magnetic Resonance Wireless Power Transfer System
abstract: Magnetic beamforming can effectively increase the power transmission efficiency for multi-coil magnetic resonance wireless power transfer (WPT) system. However, the current beamforming schemes need complicated circuits and communication protocols. In this paper, we propose a random magnetic beamforming method to achieve maximum received power. This scheme is computationally light and requires only limited feedback information. Then, a test-bed for magnetic resonance WPT is developed. The experimental results indicate that our algorithm can effectively increase the received power with a fast convergence rate.

articleTitle: Wirelessly RF-Powered Remote Push-To-Talk Button
abstract: A remote Push-To-Talk button is developed that is powered by the radio waves emitted by a body-worn radio. The button can be placed on any object, including metal ones, without losing functionality. Haptic feedback is provided, even when used wearing combat or winter gloves. The components of the remote PTT button, i.e. the push button, the RF energy harvester and the transmitter, are discussed in detail as is the demonstration of the complete wireless power and data transfer system.

articleTitle: Sub-Terahertz MSL and CPW rectenna using 303 GHz 300 kW-class Gyrotron
abstract: Sub-Terahertz 303 GHz rectenna was developed by the photolithography process and measured using a 300 kW-class Gyrotron. As a result, the maximum output power and rectenna power density for the microstrip line (MSL) and coplanar waveguide (CPW) were 17.1 mW, 3.43 kW/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and 14.5 mW, 4.87 kW/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, respectively. The RF-DC conversion efficiency was obtained 2.17 % with 342 mW input power and 130 Ω DC load. The results reveal the highest operation frequency except the photovoltaic converter.

articleTitle: A 150-W IR WPT Embedded System at 6.78-MHz for the Supply and Control of Linear Motors
abstract: This paper describes a complete system for the wireless supply and control of linear motors for industrial automation. DC power is delivered to a set of five linear motors by means of an inductive resonant wireless power link at 6.78 MHz, exploiting a GaN-HEMT full-bridge inverter and PCB high-Q resonant coils. Additional AC/DC and DC/DC converters are used for the direct connection to the power grid and to regulate a 48-V DC-link for the supply of the motor drives. The WPT link feedback control is provided with a Bluetooth connection, which is also exploited for the wireless command of the motors. A dedicated embedded system with two microcontrollers controls the entire plant, regulating the supply WPT link and the motor functionalities. The system can deliver a maximum average transferred power of 150 W, when the free space between the coils is between 15 to 20 cm.

articleTitle: A Highly Efficient Combined Power Amplifier with Branch-line Couplers
abstract: In this work, a combined power amplifier (PA) using branch-line couplers is designed over 3.4-3.8GHz covering 11% fractional bandwidth. The proposed power amplifier consists of a 5dB input coupler for input power splitting, a 10W amplifier, a 25W amplifier and a 6dB output coupler for power combination. The input matching networks and output matching networks of two harmonic-tuned mode sub-PAs are designed by using stepped-impedance matching network topology. The measured combined power amplifier shows 65%-70% drain efficiency at 46.1-46.5 dBm saturated output power, and the small signal gain is more than 10dB.

articleTitle: A Simple Technique for Characterization of WPT Coils
abstract: A conceptually simple method for measuring the inductance and AC winding resistance of coils for wireless power transfer is presented The method is a variation of well-known resonant measurement techniques, but requires only an oscilloscope, a power supply, and a small test circuit. The technique is compared to results obtained from a vector network analyzer(VNA), as well as to an in-expensive LCR meter.

articleTitle: Focused Radiative Wireless Power Transfer Experiments
abstract: In this paper we will report on first experiments carried out with pulse-delayed transmission to create focal areas or `bubbles' of high RF energy density. Through a proper transmission of delayed pulses by an array of antennas it will be possible to realize a peak power gain relative to a non-pulsed transmit (array) antenna. This gain can equal the number of array elements squared, as will be verified experimentally. Experiments are performed with an array consisting of two radiating elements. The use of the high RF energy density `bubbles' will be demonstrated by switching the focal point between two rectennas positioned in front of the transmitting array.

articleTitle: Implant Safety: Novel Mechanistic Model and Approach for Safety Assessment at WPT Frequencies
abstract: Safety assessment of active implants at frequencies used in wireless power transfer (WPT) is not yet defined by the current guidelines. A mechanistic model for elongated implants at magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) frequencies (typically 64/128 MHz) has been postulated and used as a basis for safety guidelines. However, this mechanistic model is inconsistent with the behavior observed at WPT frequencies. In this study, we propose a new mechanistic model applicable to a wide range of frequencies. Based on this model, the problem of assessing implant safety can be decomposed into separate, approachable steps. To validate the approach, predictions of the mechanistic model were compared to results of numerical simulations. The impact of parameters such as tissue properties, tip shape, and insulation thickness was studied. The findings may be applicable to the formulation of safety standards for implant wearers exposed to electromagnetic fields (EMF) at WPT frequencies.

articleTitle: Wireless Power Transfer Link for RFID Telemetry System Applied to Laboratory Rodent Monitoring
abstract: Monitoring small animal to collect telemetry during their movement is a challenging task, as the body displacement tend to impact greatly the field distribution. A power transfer scheme based on complementary split ring resonator is demonstrated here for UHF RFID reader-tag link rodent telemetry application. It is shown that the operation of the tag is maintained in all the region of the cage where the animal can move. Thanks to an adequate ground plane, the wearable tag antenna is minimally effected by the presence of the biological tissues. The map of the efficiency along the cage surface was derived from multiple simulations and measurements. It results a minimum efficiency of an order of magnitude higher than required, and a maximum of 1.8% while the tag is worn by the animal.

articleTitle: System Level Efficiency Analysis for Regulated RF Near Field Coupling
abstract: RF near field coupling systems offer the potential for very small coil area with high efficiency. However, little previous effort has been made in quantifying the various sources of loss in regulated RF near field coupling systems. This paper identifies the significant sources of loss in RF near field coupling and proposes a method of calculating the power loss without need for extensive simulation. This paper also proposes a model for the RF diode switching loss based on a machine learning algorithm, demonstrating a new approach to simply evaluate the diode switching loss.The proposed analysis is compared with measured data for a RF near field coupling system, showing good correlation between the proposed analysis and the measured results. In addition, the various sources of loss in RF near field coupling were compared and avenues for improving the efficiency in terms of the demonstrated analysis are discussed.

articleTitle: Effect of Detuning on the Performance of DR-Loaded Split Cavity Resonator Based Wireless Power Transfer Scheme
abstract: A wireless power transfer system employing split cavity and dielectric resonator is reported in this article. An important component for faithful operation of the system is the tuning of the suitable cavity and DR modes. However, to consider practical limitations and experimental tolerance, the impact of various practical detuning is thoroughly investigated in this paper. It is shown that the maximum detuning that can be tolerated is proportional to the square of the coupling coefficient. Results obtained are crucial as fabrication/material mismatch is unavoidable in practical realization of such system. Present study exhibits robustness of the DR-loaded SCR based WPT scheme, currently under realization. Verification using measurements will be presented in the conference.

articleTitle: Dielectric Loss Evaluation in Wireless Power Transmission using Parallel Four Lines
abstract: This paper evaluates the maximum transmission efficiency in dielectric of wireless power transmission (WPT) system using parallel four lines. Simulation results showed that, the transmission efficiency decreased greatly in case of the length of parallel four lines exceeds 20 m, but the transmitter coil which was within 20 m is hardly affected by the dielectric. Also, the effective range of the lateral misalignment in the dielectric was almost the same performances as compared with that in the air. Segmentation of the feeder is also discussed as a promising solution to combat the dielectric loss.

articleTitle: On the Outage of Wireless Powered Communications with Spatially Random Sensors
abstract: This paper analytically investigates the performance of a wireless powered communication system, where multiple sensors powered by multiple dedicated power beacons (PBs) communicate with an access point. Specifically, we consider a harvest-then-transmit multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communication system, where in each time frame, the sensors first collect energy from the surrounding PBs, and the sensor with the highest signal-to-interference ratio (SIR) to the access point is scheduled according to opportunistic scheduling strategy. The locations of PBs, sensors and interferers are characterized by stochastic geometry tools. Under this architecture, the outage probability of information transmission is investigated, assuming the CCI can be approximated by a Gamma distributed variable. Numerical results validate the analysis and show the impacts of the density and transmit power of terminals on the system performance.

articleTitle: A Simple High-Efficiency Rectifier for Low Power Harvesting
abstract: This paper reports a simple rectifier featuring a relatively high efficiency in connection with low input power. The measured RF-DC conversion efficiency reaches 30% at -20 dBm input power level, which, to the best knowledge of the authors, represents the highest record among all the reported works so far for this power range. The Bode-Fano criterion is employed to achieve the high energy conversion efficiency. Such rectifiers are especially useful for wire-less energy harvesting.

articleTitle: Size-Reduced Evanescent Mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide Filter with Mixed-Coupled CSRRs
abstract: In this paper, a size-reduced evanescent mode substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) bandpass filter loaded with mixed-coupled complementary split-ring resonators (CSRRs) pair is presented. In the conventional SIW-CSRR resonator with face-to-face CSRRs, a transmission zero (TZ) at the upper stopband can be generated by the mixed coupling between the SIW and CSRRs. Meanwhile, contributed from the evanescent mode characteristics, the electrical size of the resonator is miniaturized, so that its physical size can be reduced as well. By adding a slot between the splits of the two CSRRs to combine them together, a dual-mode resonator is proposed, in which the cross coupling scheme is formed to generate an extra TZ at the lower stopband of the proposed resonator to improve its selectivity performance notably. Meanwhile, owing to the proposed dual-mode resonator performing evanescent mode operation, it can keep miniaturized size simultaneously. To verify the aforementioned idea, a size-reduced bandpass filter based on the proposed resonator is realized. Experimental results shows that good performance and compact size are achieved, which indicates the proposed work is promising in practical microwave applications.

articleTitle: Novel Approach for Compliance Testing of WPT Systems with Basic Restrictions
abstract: The magnetic fields (MF) generated in close proximity to high power wireless power transfer (WPT) systems generally exceed exposure limits and might also violate basic restrictions (BR). However, there are as yet no available standards describing methods to measure the MF generated by WPT systems. In this study, a new method for demonstration of compliance with the BR in the close proximity to sources at frequencies from 3 kHz to 10 MHz is proposed. This approach mitigates overestimation by incident field assessment in strong field gradients close to WPT systems. The spatial peak MF amplitude and gradient generated by WPT systems are measured with a field gradient probe at the closest location to the source. The induced fields and absorbed power are then calculated on the basis of specific transformation functions for testing of compliance with the BR of all international safety guidelines.

articleTitle: Shielding Effectiveness and Figure of Merit of Ferrite Shielded Coils
abstract: In this paper is presented a study of the influence of the shielding ferrite on the performance of a Wireless Power Transfer WPT system. Due to the wide variability of the magnetic parameters in the commercial ferrite samples a measurement procedure to assess the correct value of the magnetic permeability vs frequency is adopted. The coupling and the shielding effectiveness are evaluated in a sample case.

articleTitle: Rectenna with Enhanced Aperture Efficiency and a Bi-directional Pattern for Ambient RF Energy Harvesting
abstract: This paper introduces a novel rectenna with a double-sided ground plane microstiip antenna that has a bidirectional radiation pattern for ambient RadioFrequency (RF) energy harvesting. The microstrip antenna has a supplementary slot that enhances the aperture efficiency of a conventional rectangular patch antenna from 50% to 72% in simulation and allows for a high gain bi-directional pattern. With a maximum experimental gain of 7 dBi, the proposed rectenna can capture as much ambient RF power as a patch antenna and rectify it with an efficiency of 25.8% for a 0.15 nW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> power density, while being less sensitive to the energy source location. By duplicating the rectenna, two complementary radiation patterns can be obtained allowing incoming RF radiations with four different orientations to be collected.

articleTitle: A Power Scavenging Current Transformer to Remotely Power ‘Bird on Wire’ Sensors in Grid Monitoring
abstract: This paper presents the design of a current transformer that is used for scavenging power from an 60 Hz ac transmission line. The primary goal of the design is to maximize the scavenged power under minimum line current conditions of a few amperes to power sensor in a smart grid network. Impedance matching is shown to be critical to obtain maximum power. An experimental test bed was setup to verify the design. A current transformer with a ferrite core was used with 450 turns of 28 AWG copper wire can deliver 9.5 mW of power at a line current of 1.54 A. The load circuit consists of a bridge rectifier and a low drop-out regulator designed to charge a 4.0 V NiMH battery pack.

articleTitle: Demonstration of long distance transmission with rectenna array using 300kW-class 28GHz Gyrotron
abstract: To demonstrate the high-power millimeter wave WPT, the class F-load rectenna array was used with a 28 GHz 300 kW-class Gyrotron. As a result, the output DC power and the transmission efficiency for 0.9 m distance and 52.9 kW input were respectively 1.05 W and 2.30 %. Results reveal that 90 m transmission distance was obtained considering the attenuator. In terms of the input power and the operation frequency, the present work showed the remarkable WPT demonstration as compared with the previous studies.

articleTitle: Scalable Model of Planar Square One-turn Inductors for Wireless Power Transfer Applications
abstract: This paper describes an scalable Planar-Square One-turn Inductor model valid for estimating the quality factor and the input impedance of the inductor up to its self-resonance frequency (SRF). Therefore it can be used to guide the optimized process of the inductive link and the power stage of the WPT system without full-wave electromagnetic simulation. The proposed scalar model is analytic, its circuit components have physical meaning, and its model parameters can be extracted from empirical or simulated data. This model was assessed by full-wave EM simulation, the results was consistent the values predicted by the lumped model.

articleTitle: Nonlinear two-step simulation model of a resonant converter for IPT Systems
abstract: The electrification of the automotive industry brings the promising inductive power transfer (IPT) technology in the focus of future battery charging applications. However, establishing IPT systems is only possible if similar efficiency, compared to conductive charging, can be achieved. Hence, the design of IPT systems needs to be further examined. This paper presents a novel two-step simulation method of resonant converters for IPT systems. First, the magnetic domain, respectively the coil system, is simulated with finite element analysis (FEA), where saturation effects, misalignment and the geometric design can be taken into account. In the second step, the results are imported into a network circuit domain to analyze the complete resonant converter, with the possibility of studying dynamic effects. Main advantage of this method is the consideration of nonlinearities from the time consuming FEA in the faster network circuit domain, which leads to more precise results while requiring less simulation time.

articleTitle: Designing a Compact and High-efficiency Rectifier with a Multilayer Substrate Filter
abstract: We proposed a multilayer substrate filter composed of a microstrip line and substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) for the output filter of the rectifier to reduce the size of the rectifier circuit in the previous study. In this paper, we improve the multilayer substrate filter and design the filter for the rectifier input filter. Moreover, we place these filters in the rectifier, simulate its rectification characteristic and compare it with the conventional rectifier. As a result, we achieve downsizing the circuit area and improving its efficiency.

articleTitle: Optimization and Analysis of Coplanar Double-Repeater Used in Dynamic Wireless Charging
abstract: It is shown that the distance of wireless power transfer (WPT) can be significantly increased by placing intermediate coils (repeaters) between transmitter and receiver. While in common cases, repeaters are placed near the middle of the gap between them, which puts limits on the application of WPT system with repeaters. At the same time, misalignment between transmitter and receiver greatly affects the performance of the system. This paper proposes a coplanar double-repeater (CPDR). By parameter optimization, the feasibility of biased repeater and effects of improving misalignment tolerance and efficiency are verified. The biased repeater is applied so that the proposed repeater can be used in dynamic charging for EVs. The repeater is placed close to receiver and they are integrated into an equivalent receiver. To improve the power transmission ability, the frequency of the integrated system is adjusted. The performance of the proposed repeater in dynamic charging system is validated by simulation.

articleTitle: Highly-Sensitive Diode Rectifier with Self-Compensated Reflection Based on Novel Operation Principle
abstract: Highly sensitive rectifier based on a new operation principle is presented. The rectifier modified from a standard single-shunt diode rectifier employs a series inductor. The inductor is optimized so as to resonate with the diode parasitic capacitance, thereby enhancing the induced electromotive force of the inductor to effectively reduce the threshold voltage of the diode. The resonance also leads to self-compensation of the reflection, enabling to make full use of the weak input RF signal. Despite the simple circuit configuration, the minimum RF input power required for rectification is reduced by more than two orders of magnitude. A prototype 2.45-GHz rectifier was fabricated using commercial packaged diode, demonstrating 28% RF-DC conversion efficiency and 5% reflectance for RF input power of -20 dBm.

articleTitle: Design of Standard-compliant Non-galvanic HF RFID Cards
abstract: Non-galvanic HF RFID cards do not have a galvanic connection between the card's body and the Integrated Circuit (IC), in order to reduce production costs and increase card's robustness. These non-galvanic cards are more complex than conventional ones since they have more parameters. Currently, there exists no systematic design method to ensure their standard-compliance. In this work, we formulate a constrained optimization problem to calculate the parameters of such non-galvanic card that lead to a standard-compliant card, in addition to verifying the results through standardized measurements on one type of these non-galvanic cards denoted as booster-based card.

articleTitle: Class B* - A New High Efficiency RF DC/DC Converter Concept Using Second Harmonic Generation/Injection
abstract: RF DC/DC converters typically treat power amplifier and rectifier separately. This paper presents a novel approach to designing converters based on the interaction between amplifier and rectifier. By utilising the second harmonic power generated in the rectifier to realise second harmonic injection to the power amplifier, both can be operated at high efficiency. This waveform engineering based concept is explored mathematically and then simulated. Based on this analysis, a class $\mathrm{B}^{*}$ rectifier based on a 0.25 $\mu \mathrm{m}6\mathrm{x}80\mu \mathrm{m}\mathrm{G}\mathrm{a}\mathrm{N}$ HEMT is measured using a load-pull/source-pull measurement system to emulate the required harmonic impedance environment. The resulting voltage and current waveforms are de-embedded to the intrinsic current generator plane and analysed, confirming the ability of this kind of rectifier to provide beneficial second harmonic injection to a power amplifier. The rectifier‘s efficiency is measured to be more than 90% over an input power range of 20 dB if the generated second harmonic is taken into account.

articleTitle: Enhancement Method of Efficiency and Working Range in Bio-Implant Wireless Power Transfer
abstract: An effective control method with improved energy efficiency and extended working range based on 1X/2X reconfigurable rectifier is presented for wireless power transfer in implantable medical devices (IMDs). Compared to the conventional method that fixes the duty cycle of the reconfigurable rectifier to be around 50%, the proposed method optimizes the duty cycle for different coupling and loading conditions, so the system efficiency is significantly improved and the workable coupling and loading range is greatly extended. Simulation results in a commercial 0.18 μm CMOS technology validate the proposed method.
